about.title: Modesto Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Work in Modesto spans a lot of ground: food processing plants, warehouses, farm operations across Stanislaus County, construction sites, and the delivery and service routes along Coffee Road, Oakdale Road, Tully Road and Briggsmore Avenue. An injury in any of these settings raises the same first question — what are you actually entitled to? Under California law, workers' compensation usually covers medical care and part of your lost wages no matter who was at fault, and it is normally your only claim against your employer. But if someone outside your company caused the harm — a subcontractor, the owner of the property you were working on, the maker of equipment that failed, or another driver who hit your work vehicle — a separate third-party injury claim may be open to you as well. That second path matters for people who drive for work; Modesto recorded 1,365 injury collisions in 2025, and some of those happened on the clock. LawProactive is a free service that pairs you with an independent Modesto attorney who can sort out which claims apply.

items.question: I was hit on Briggsmore Avenue while making deliveries for my employer. Is that a workers' comp case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. Because you were working, workers' compensation should cover your medical care and part of your lost wages regardless of who caused the crash. If the other driver was at fault, you may also have a separate third-party injury claim against that driver, which follows California's two-year deadline. An attorney can help you pursue both without one undermining the other.

items.question: Do I have to report a workplace injury right away?
items.answer: California asks you to notify your employer within 30 days of the injury. Reporting sooner is better, and putting it in writing helps create a clear record. Your employer cannot legally fire, demote or punish you for reporting an injury or filing a claim.

items.question: My injury was caused by a machine at a Modesto processing plant. Can I sue anyone?
items.answer: Generally you cannot sue your own employer because workers' comp is the exclusive remedy against them. However, if the machine was defectively designed or manufactured, or a separate contractor serviced it improperly, a third-party claim against that company may be possible. An independent attorney can review the equipment and maintenance history to see whether that path exists.
